summary: A one-keyword, rules-clean probe that still targets 5 live sliding FA3 shapes (decode_16/32, verify_1/16/32; sliding decode_1 now bypasses FA3). Shapes are config-branched and independent, so one run is readable per shape without companions. The headline 'faster' expectations are probably wrong: the profile suggests the split is worth more than its combine. Run it as a cheap, readable test of whether splitting pays for its combine on sliding layers, not as a likely gain.
justification: Mechanism, partly right: under varlen dynamic split an explicit num_splits is only a cap (LESSONS; the decode_layer fa3-full-single-split-probe review). But a cap of 1 does bind. Split=false, so the main kernel writes bf16 directly and FlashAttnFwdCombine is skipped. That is the one case where the 'only a cap' hold reasoning that parked fa3-num-splits-sliding does not apply. prepare_varlen_num_blocks will almost certainly still launch, because cu_seqlens_q (varlen) plus a local window needs the tile scheduler's semaphore and the dynamic path. So the most that can be saved is the combine: 3.1-4.2 us per shape in the current-best profile (decode_16 3.2, decode_32 3.3, verify_1 3.7, verify_16 4.2, verify_32 4.1 us), not the 4-5 us the hypothesis claims. The hypothesis's '~2.3 us per launch' also does not match the measured combine. Cost side, the weakest link: the claim that one CTA streams a 2,048-token window (16-17 blocks x 128 rows x 128 B = 256 KB at page size 1) 'in a few microseconds' is not supported. In the same-run profiles the sliding FA3 main kernel grows as the tile count rises and FA3's dynamic pick has fewer splits per tile: about 8.2 us at decode_1 (2 tiles, many splits), 9.9 us at decode_16 (32 tiles), 13.3 us at decode_32 (64 tiles). That fits roughly 7 us fixed plus ~0.75 us per serial 128-row block. At 16-17 serial blocks per CTA that predicts a ~19-20 us main kernel. Against 9.9+3.2 = 13.1 us at decode_16 that is a ~+5-7 us loss, and against 13.3+3.3 = 16.6 us at decode_32 a ~+2-4 us loss. Independent evidence: the Triton fused sliding kernel took 17.4 us at S=4 and 28.8 us at S=2 (sliding-single-launch-fused-attention), so long single-CTA page-size-1 gathers are latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound. The grid falls to 32/64 CTAs (B*Hkv, one packed-GQA m-block) on 132 SMs, which is far from the 1.6-3.7 us floors, so this cannot be a bandwidth win. Expected table vs TASK: (1) 'sliding decode_1 flat' is moot. Master routes batch-1 decode to _sliding_fused_kernel, so that shape never reaches FA3 and is a byte-identical control. (2) 'sliding verify_1 flat' is the biggest risk. It runs 2 CTAs x ~17 serial blocks against a 7.7 us split main kernel plus 3.7 us combine, so expect perhaps +8-12 us on a ~17 us shape. At weight 46 the sliding shape dominates the verify_1 load (46x17 vs 16x30 us), so this alone could cost several percent of geomean. (3) decode_32/verify_32 are the only rows where a gain is plausible, if FA3's dynamic pick there is already ~1-2 splits. (4) Full rows flat is correct: the change is gated on window != 0. Net: likely below 1.293x overall, possibly with a small win at batch 32.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate: sliding decode_1 no longer calls FA3 (kernel_fn returns _sliding_forward for window && batch==1 && q_len==1), so the hypothesis's decode_1 expectation is void. That row is a pure drift control. Sliding verify_1 still goes through FA3 and becomes the only batch-1 sliding row affected.

fused-preattention-triton: it precedes FA3 on the same stream and writes q/k/v, but it does not change FA3's split decision or the window traffic. It adds no interaction beyond a fixed ~1.7-4 us in front, which is identical in both arms.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: they touch full layers only (paired = window == 0 and ...), and the sliding call stays unpaired with metadata None. No interaction. The full rows are controls.

Not landed but relevant: fa3-scheduler-metadata-side-stream (running) touches the same sliding FA3 call's schedule. If it lands first, its metadata must be built with num_splits=1 (or this change must drop it), or the cap and the precomputed schedule disagree. Do not stack the two without rebuilding.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change branches only on config, and every scored shape is an independent kernel_fn call, so one run already gives a separate same-run answer for each of the five affected sliding shapes, with the full rows and sliding decode_1 as unchanged drift controls. Read each shape's FA3 main-kernel time and the absence of FlashAttnFwdCombine/prepare in top_kernels, not the headline. No landed hypothesis changes the sliding FA3 split path, so an ab-revert has nothing to isolate. A batch-gated variant (num_splits=1 only at batch>=32) can be decided from this run's per-shape rows without another run. Spending a second check on it beforehand would duplicate information. If the run shows wins only at batch 32, mint that gate as a stacked follow-up.
rules_flags: None. num_splits=1 attends the same full 2,048-token window (no block skipping), adds no host sync, caches nothing derived from inputs and keeps the FP8 E4M3 query/KV path. Removing the fp32 split combine only changes the reduction order, so numerics can only improve.
Implementation note, not a rule problem: pass num_splits only on the window != 0 FA3 call and leave the full-layer call byte-identical. Otherwise the full rows stop being controls.
open_questions: Does the judge's sgl_kernel FA3 still launch prepare_varlen_num_blocks with num_splits=1 + cu_seqlens_q + local window? Expected yes (semaphore), which caps the saving at the 3.1-4.2 us combine. Confirm from top_kernels.
Sliding verify_1 (2 CTAs, ~17 serial blocks at q_len 8) is the likely large loss the hypothesis marks 'flat'. If it regresses heavily, treat the run as information and never promote it whole.

What split count does FA3 pick dynamically today at sliding decode_32/verify_32? If it is already 1-2, those rows should be ~flat-to-faster by ~3 us. That is the only place this could become a gated keeper.
Attention has 2 checks left today. Given the likely net loss, churn may reasonably rank this below any candidate with a positive expected headline. That is a scheduling call, not a reason to hold.
